# R284GB — Uniform all-q first-edge barrier in the two-heavy sector

Date: 2026-11-24 Asia/Shanghai.
Research mode: informed portable Enterprise Math; frozen R284CO/R284FM four-phase binary observer model.
Status: AUTHOR_DERIVED / EXACT_FINITE_CERTIFICATE / NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED.
Researcher-ID: EM-DIRECT-77946D; own native Activity: RA-82630CAF8F9ECE1B7337CC7F. No shared CLAIM, formal Result or Review is asserted.

## Theorem (conditional but uniform in q)

Fix four cyclic distinct binary phase words c0,c1,c2,c3. Each edge attempts every changing bit once, with at most q omissions; omitted updates from earlier cycles may persist. Each read suffers at most one adversarial bit flip; the decoder is stateless and non-atomic publishing must not recognize a third phase or roll a successful newer read back to an older phase. Normalize c0=0 and count the seven nonconstant coordinate types by p=1,...,7, with phase bits (0,p&1,(p>>1)&1,(p>>2)&1).

For integer q >= 5 and k in {8,9}, put n=4q+k. A histogram x=(x1,...,x7) is stable-admissible if it meets the six nominal word-distance necessities and all six exact stable residual-flow-cut separation conditions of R284FM/R284GA. Say x is two-heavy if two distinct types from {3,5,6} have x_g >= 2q+2.

**R284GB. No stable-admissible two-heavy histogram at either width n=4q+8 or n=4q+9 admits a full safe four-phase publication protocol, for any integer q>=5.**

Detailed exhaustive classification in this sector:

| Width | Stable families, by R284GA | Excluded by new first-edge prefix barrier | Remaining first-edge candidates | Excluded by R284FW second-edge theorem |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4q+8 | 7 | 6 | 1 (F0) | 1 |
| 4q+9 | 66 | 56 | 10 (F1–F10) | 10 |

Here "remaining candidate" means only that the specified necessary first-edge obstruction did not eliminate it, not that a safe write order exists. This theorem is scoped to the two-heavy sector; proving every unrestricted stable-admissible histogram is two-heavy is still open.

## Exact prefix distance via the eight-source min-cut dual

On edge i to t=(i+1) mod 4, let s_p count successfully written coordinates of type p (0 <= s_p <= x_p). Compare such an intermediate state with a fully stable state of phase j. Let ell_i(p) and ell_j(p) denote last nominal changed-edge group for p prior to phases i and j. Retain eight distinct omission-budget vertices L0..L3 and R0..R3, each with capacity q.

Create demand items:
1. If c_i(p) differs from c_j(p), each of the x_p-s_p unattempted-or-unsuccessfully-updated coordinates is a demand of weight x_p-s_p incident to both L[ell_i(p)] and R[ell_j(p)].
2. If c_t(p) differs from c_j(p), each of the s_p successful updated coordinates is a demand of weight s_p incident only to R[ell_j(p)].

For each item a, N(a) is its incident budget-vertex set. The exact minimum physical Hamming distance is

    delta(i,t,j;x,s,q) =
        max over U subset {L0,L1,L2,L3,R0,R1,R2,R3}
        ( sum over items a with N(a) subset U of weight(a) - q * |U| ).

The empty set contributes 0. This is the integral maximum-flow/minimum-cut dual of R284FT's prefix oracle: a demanded differing bit can be repaired by a legal omitted last update in either corresponding source group; a successful write can be repaired only on the target stable history side. All 256 cuts are explicit, retaining update-source provenance rather than replacing the distinct omission budgets by a single Hamming radius. Distance <=2 yields intersecting radius-one observation balls. For edge 0->1 any intersection with phase j=2 or j=3 forces forbidden third-phase recognition. Following the inherited necessary-prefix protocol, an intersection with j=1 at at most two successful writes also makes premature target recognition unsafe. The latter is checked only in the stated range.

## Uniform lifting of an ambiguity witness via omission-slot matching

Let q0=5. For a heavy pair G and base histogram x, construct the lift

    x(q)_p = x_p + 2(q-5) * indicator[p in G].

Assume a concrete prefix ambiguity at base q0, with no attempts on the as-yet-added heavy columns, and with legal omission histories on both compared physical states. Increase q to q+1 by appending two coordinates of each heavy type.

For any added heavy type whose phase bits at source i and comparison phase j agree, the two added coordinates agree automatically. If they differ, either omit the last update in source phase i's history or omit the last update in comparison phase j's history, thereby matching the physical values. These two options consume one unit respectively of slots L[ell_i(p)] and R[ell_j(p)]. There are two new coordinates for each differing heavy type. If these demand instances can be matched injectively into available L/R slots, each old history edge incurs at most one extra missed update when q grows by one. The previous physical-state pair and its Hamming distance are preserved on old coordinates, and the appended coordinates contribute zero distance. Iterate to every larger q.

For source i=0, the possible matching is exact (enumerate two options for each of at most four new differing columns):

| Heavy pair G | Liftable comparison phases j | Excluded collisions |
|---|---|---|
| {3,5} | 2,3 | j=1 |
| {3,6} | 1,2,3 | none |
| {5,6} | 1,2 | j=3 |

For instance, in {5,6} compared with j=3, four new differing columns have only the three distinct available slots L3,R2,R1, so the basic lift does not apply. The finite certificate conservatively discards any witness against a nonliftable comparison phase. New heavy coordinates are unattempted before the barrier, so the number of successful attempted writes is unchanged; hence the early j=1 restriction is preserved whenever liftable.

## Complete bounded q0=5 classification and first-edge barrier

R284GA proves a q-independent finite description of all two-heavy stable-admissible histograms. For G in {{3,5},{3,6},{5,6}} write x_p=2q*indicator[p in G]+z_p with z_g>=2 for g in G and sum z=k. Enumerate each weak composition of k-4 into seven nonnegative parts, adding 2 to each heavy coordinate: 630 offsets for k=8 and 1386 for k=9. Apply R284GA's six nominal distance predicates plus the six exact eight-vertex stable cuts. There are 7 and 66 survivors, with group breakdown (3,1,3) and (28,10,28). At q=5 directly re-evaluate all six original cuts for each survivor.

On the first publication edge 0->1, only types {1,3,5,7} may change. The attempt-count state is a monotone integer lattice. Cap each updated heavy type at 8 attempts (its base q=5 multiplicity is >=12); cap the remaining types at their actual unchanged multiplicity. Starting with zero attempts, visit each reachable state. For every next attempted-count state enumerate all legal allocations of missed attempted writes with sum<=5. Mark a state forbidden only if the exact 256-cut formula finds minimum phase-to-phase distance<=2 for an applicable liftable phase j in the table above; for j=1 require at most two successful writes. Otherwise permit that state.

Out of the 73 stable families, 62 admit no path of permitted states reaching an updated-heavy count of 8. Every full attempt ordering must cross a forbidden prefix before that boundary. Each forbidden prefix and its real base omission witness lifts to the same attempted-count prefix for all q>=5 by the slot-matching lemma. The remaining 11 are *exactly* F0..F10 specified in R284FW, one at width 4q+8 and ten at 4q+9. Existing R284FW shows a second-edge 1->2 prefix barrier for those 11 for every q>=2. This completes the stated conditional theorem.

The checker examines 2016 offsets and all 73 stable cases, visits 411 safe first-edge lattice nodes and identifies 257 forbidden neighbor states across the cases. Additional complete fixed-box regression runs for q=6,7,11 leave the same 62 obstructed cases. These samples check the implementation, whereas the all-q assertion uses R284GA's affine exhaustive classification plus the combinatorial omission-slot lift.

## Reproducibility and evidence

Self-contained standard-library exact-integer checker:
research_notes/portable_direct/R284GB_twoheavy_uniform_first_edge_barrier.py

Run: python3 R284GB_twoheavy_uniform_first_edge_barrier.py

Observed locally before Source publication:

    width=4q+8: stable=7 capped_edge_survivors=1
    width=4q+9: stable=66 capped_edge_survivors=10
    PASS stable=7+66, first-edge candidate families=1+10, obstructed=62, base_safe_nodes=411, base_bad_nodes=257
    PASS q=6,7,11 lifted obstacle regressions; all-q from omission-slot lemma

The 256-cut dual was independently compared in an additional 1000 random finite integer instances to the inherited integral-flow implementation; no mismatch was observed. No additional ordinary analytic approximation is used. The result is a scientific theorem of an auxiliary binary observer model, not a change to Enterprise Math's P000 six-native-axis foundation, ACTIVE worldview, or native X6 geometry. Retaining distinct last-write sources and exact residual budgets implements the applicable residual-preservation method; no native BRC numerical interface is invoked.

- R284GA two-heavy converse: awdawmip/enterprise-math@0c3284aec3e378b384beb43f232018d7978455da:research_notes/portable_direct/R284GA_TWO_HEAVY_UNIFORM_STABLE_CONVERSE_20261124.md
- R284FW family second-edge obstruction: awdawmip/enterprise-math@bfbeefc839da0fb1b9d6d87db10c531b1f0f5cbc:research_notes/portable_direct/R284FW_ALL_Q_PARAMETRIC_FIRST_EDGE_SURVIVOR_SECOND_EDGE_OBSTRUCTION_20261123.md
- R284FT exact prefix-flow interface as cited by R284FW/R284FV. The present script directly reconstructs its exact integral min-cut equivalent.

## Unresolved question and next independent unit

Prove or refute: for q>=5, any unrestricted seven-pattern histogram of width 4q+8 or 4q+9 passing all six nominal distance and six exact stable residual-cut inequalities has at least two of x3,x5,x6 >=2q+2. This is the only remaining classification premise before combining R284GB with the earlier lower bound and 4q+10 Gray construction to obtain a full all-q capacity theorem (plus already-proved q=2..14). If the premise is false, retain the explicit non-heavy witness and examine its first-edge prefix conditions as a distinct next route.
